_comment: Shared vectors for how a released drag on a Drawer is judged.
Read by coui_core (CoreDragVelocityTracker, CoreDrawerContract.dismissesOnRelease),
coui_flutter (a real drag on the bottom sheet), coui_web (the same chain the pointer
handler runs) and a real-Chrome probe of the Web drawer, so a rule that changes on one
platform fails on the other.
UNITS. Every velocity is logical pixels per SECOND. A browser stamps events in
milliseconds and its deltas are per millisecond, so a speed of 1.2 px/ms is 1200 px/s.
tracker.cases: samples are [timeMs, positionPx] along one axis, in the order a pointer
reports them (the press, then each move; the lift is not a sample). pxPerSec is the signed
velocity (positive = position growing) as of readAtMs — the moment the question is asked,
which for a release is the lift — or as of the last sample when readAtMs is absent. A stroke
whose newest sample follows a silence longer than stoppedGapMs reports 0 (the pointer had
stopped), and so does a read more than stoppedGapMs after the newest sample.
release.cases: dragDistance is how far the panel moved toward the edge it hides behind
(negative = back toward the docked edge); velocity is signed the same way (positive =
toward that edge); velocityThreshold, where absent, is the contract default (400 px/s).
gestures: an end-to-end drag on a bottom sheet whose panel is `extent` px tall, moving
`travel` px toward the edge over `durationMs` at constant speed (so the speed is
travel/durationMs*1000 px/s), then, when `holdMs` is present, holding still for `holdMs`
before the lift. `dismisses` is what the sheet does on release. The speeds
keep a wide margin either side of the 400 px/s threshold: a probe on a loaded machine
dispatches its events late, which can only make a flick slower.

cases.name: a steady flick at 1.2 px/ms is 1200 px/s
a slow drag at 0.2 px/ms is 200 px/s
moving toward smaller positions is negative
two samples are a direction
one sample is no direction
samples at one instant are no direction
a jittery stroke is its trend, not its last step
only the last 100 ms count, the boundary sample included
a long silence before the newest sample is a stop, not a fling
a lift 30 ms after the last move is still a flick
a lift exactly at the stopped gap is still a flick
a lift just past the stopped gap is a stop, not a fling
a long hold before the lift is not a fling
a pause in the middle forgets the motion before it
a clock that has run for hours loses no precision
an out-of-order sample is dropped, not reordered
exactly the threshold share of the panel dismisses
a pixel short of the threshold share snaps back
the share is the panel's, not the screen's
a drag back toward the docked edge never dismisses
a panel with no extent has covered nothing
a zero threshold is met by any release
a short drag released as a flick dismisses
exactly the velocity threshold is a flick
a pixel per second under the velocity threshold is not
a short slow drag snaps back
a long drag at rest dismisses exactly as before speed existed
a speed away from the edge never dismisses
a long drag released moving back still dismisses by distance
speed with nothing moved is not a throw
speed from a panel pulled back past its dock is not a throw
a caller's own velocity threshold replaces the default
the same speed under the default threshold does not
0.5 px/ms is 500 px/s and dismisses
0.3 px/ms is 300 px/s and does not
a short quick flick dismisses although it covers well under half
a short slow drag snaps back
a long slow drag dismisses by distance
a quick flick toward the docked edge does nothing
a quick flick held still before the lift snaps back
